title: Underived-to-derived procyclic bar augmentation for noncomplete norm scalars
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology. Let $A(S)=C(S,\Omega)$ on the coherent profinite site [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], with all continuous maps, in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Put $H=\mathbf Z_\ell$ with its inverse-limit topology, acting trivially on $A$ [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Use ordinary internal $A$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and their ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $U_A^q$ be the internal module with sections $C(S\times H^q,\Omega)$ and the trivial-action inhomogeneous additive-group differential
$$(df)(s;t_1,\ldots,t_{q+1})=f(s;t_2,\ldots,t_{q+1})+\sum_{i=1}^q(-1)^if(s;t_1,\ldots,t_i+t_{i+1},\ldots,t_{q+1})+(-1)^{q+1}f(s;t_1,\ldots,t_q).$$
Set $d^0=0$ and $U_A^q=0$ for $q<0$. Write $A[\underline H^q]$ for the free internal module on $S\mapsto C(S,H^q)$. Evaluation identifies $U_A^q$ with the underived internal module Hom from $A[\underline H^q]$ to $A$. Let
$$\mathscr B_A(H)=\operatorname{Tot}_{q\geq0}R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline H^q],A[0])$$
with the compatible nonnegative resolution model of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar]. For an equivariant injective resolution $A\to I^\bullet$, the maps induced by $A\to I^0$ in each bar degree specify the canonical resolution augmentation
$$j_A:Q(U_A^\bullet)\longrightarrow\mathscr B_A(H).$$
This actual morphism is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_A)$. It is independent of compatible resolution choices and its degree-zero augmentation is the identity on $A$. This does not assert that each individual underived internal-Hom term is acyclic. No completion, solidification, or finite-subextension-valued replacement of $A$ is used.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar] to choose a compatible nonnegative model. Apply [lem-sfb-profinite-free-hom-resolution-evaluation] to the condensed ring $A$, the module $N=A$ and the profinite parameter $P=H^p$: evaluation on the tautological free generator over $S\times H^p$ identifies the underived row $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline H^p],A)(S)$ with $U_A^p(S)=C(S\times H^p,\Omega)$, compatibly with restriction in $S$. By the same node, precomposition with $A[v]$ for a continuous $v:H^{p+1}\to H^p$ is pullback along $1_S\times v$; taking for $v$ the deletion of an end coordinate and the addition of adjacent coordinates gives the displayed bar faces. The action on $A$ is trivial, so the first face has no action factor and $d^0=0$. No Cech-vanishing assertion is used.

proof.text: In that model let $V_{J,q}^p=H^q(D_J^{p,\bullet})$. For $q>0$, [lem-sfb-procyclic-positive-function-cohomology-effacement] makes every horizontal cocycle locally a boundary after restriction to an open $K\subseteq H$. Apply [lem-sfb-internal-bar-row-finite-index-transfer] to the same resolution: on horizontal cohomology transfer composed with restriction is $[H:K]1$. The integer $[H:K]$ is nonzero and invertible in $\Omega$, so multiplication by its inverse constant function kills the original class locally. Every section of the cohomology sheaf is locally represented by a cocycle (the quotient is by the sheaf image). Refining the finite covers therefore proves $H^p(V_{H,q}^\bullet)=0$ for every $p\geq0,q>0$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-bar-augmentation-row-comparison] with $R=A$, $G=H$ and trivial module $N=A$. Step 2 verifies its row hypothesis for every compatible resolution. It makes the total map with $(p,0)$ component induced by $A\to I^0$ a quasi-isomorphism. Under step 1 this map is precisely the actual $j_A$ specified in the statement, so its localization is an isomorphism.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: scalar analytic base below the tame-boundary polynomial bar calculation; agent expansion, not a theorem asserted by the blueprint. Repaired short assembly, step 3

proof.text: The resolution-lift, total-homotopy and compatible-model conclusions of [lem-sfb-bar-augmentation-row-comparison] give independence for the same augmentation. Its degree-zero normalization gives $H^0(j_A)=1_A$: $H^0$ as a parameter is a point and invariants of the trivial action are $A$. Empty test spaces have zero sections, negative terms vanish, and the first-quadrant totals have finite diagonals. All coefficients throughout are the all-continuous noncomplete $A$.
